flashcards.front: What is the primary threat vector for Security Foundations (CIA Triad)?
flashcards.back_definition: Adversaries exploit single-point database failure paths on sensitive data servers to bypass standard perimeter security controls.
flashcards.back_example: Example: Asset ID: Server-01 | Integrity check: FAIL | Impact: HIGH
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse this threat with other layers (like physical breaches or certificate revocations) which target different assets.
flashcards.back_hook: Recall: single-point database failure paths is the unlocked door; sensitive data servers is what the attacker wants to steal.

flashcards.front: How does the security team mitigate Security Foundations (CIA Triad) threats?
flashcards.back_definition: Deploying and enforcing Defense-in-Depth layers directly hardens sensitive data servers and blocks unauthorized connections.
flashcards.back_example: Action: Update security configurations to require Defense-in-Depth layers.
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse mitigation (actively blocking the exploit) with detection (simply logging or alerting the event).
flashcards.back_hook: Mitigation is the shield; detection is the security camera.

flashcards.front: How do analysts detect exploitation of Security Foundations (CIA Triad)?
flashcards.back_definition: By auditing event data and implementing logic flags built to alert on quantitative risk assessment matrices.
flashcards.back_example: Syslog trace: Asset ID: Server-01 | Integrity check: FAIL | Impact: HIGH
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse signature-based detection (matching known strings) with anomaly-based detection (mapping dynamic standard deviations).
flashcards.back_hook: Detection is looking for the fingerprint left behind by the threat.
